title: UVM: Fault-Injection Callback
constraints: Write `class invert_callback extends my_callback`, overriding `pre_drive(cb_item item)` so it inverts every bit of `item.data` (`item.data = ~item.data;`).
`cb_driver` already calls every callback registered on it (via `` `uvm_do_callbacks ``) right before driving each item, so your override changes what actually gets driven onto the bus.

The hidden test registers your callback on the driver only partway through the run, so the same driver instance must behave differently before and after `uvm_callbacks#(cb_driver, my_callback)::add(...)` is called — you don't call `add` yourself.
The UVM library is the Verilator-compatible chipsalliance/uvm-verilator (UVM 2017), and building it takes about a minute.
hints: A callback method is just a virtual function on a `uvm_callback` subclass — you don't need `uvm_object_utils` or a factory type for it here, since the hidden test constructs it with a plain `new()`.
`item` is the exact same object the driver is about to send, so mutating `item.data` in place is enough — there's nothing to return.

examples.check: with no callback registered, the driver passes data through unchanged
examples.title: before registration
examples.expected: the monitor observes the original data

examples.check: once the callback is registered, every item is inverted before it's driven
examples.title: after registration
examples.input: 15 more items, your callback now attached
examples.expected: the monitor observes ~data for each one
